newsitem.title: USA: Broad tech rally lifts Nasdaq to new high.
newsitem.headline: Broad tech rally lifts Nasdaq to new high.

text.p: Fueled by a broad rally in technology issues, Nasdaq shares soared to a new summit on Tuesday, closing above 1400 for the first time.

The Nasdaq composite index surged 19.48 points or 1.40 percent to close unofficially at 1409.20, breaking the previous record high set on Friday. Nasdaq shares have made gains in seven of the previous 10 sessions. Advancing issues outpaced declining issues 2255 to 2085 on total volume of 647.4 million shares.

Traders said Tuesday's rally touched almost every sector of the technology group, from computer companies to chip stocks to networking firms. Even disk drive makers rebounded Tuesday, recovering slightly from recent losses that were driven by fears that disk drive prices will decline further.

"People are coming to their senses. These things tend to get overdone. They get oversold and then they come back. Basically, inflation is slow. Earnings have been great. It's just a great environment for tech stocks," said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president at Unterberg Harris.
The biggest winners on Tuesday included 3Com Corp, up 3-1/2 to 46-3/4; Intel Corp, up 6-2/16 to 169-5/16; and Dell Computer Corp,up six to 113-1/4.
